\section{The combinatorial scan, composition by composition}
\label{app:compositions}

Every one of the 82 object compositions the combinatorial scan of
Section~\ref{sec:combinatorial} reaches, with whether a published search scans a mass built from
those object types. This is the row-by-row form of Table~\ref{tab:compgap}: the
25 covered and 57 uncovered entries below are that table's columns,
so its counts can be checked rather than taken on trust.

\emph{cat.} is the number of exclusive multiplicity categories the composition occurs in, and
\emph{looks} the independent looks the scan spends on it, summed over those categories. Coverage
is assigned as generously as can be defended --- any published ATLAS search scanning a mass of those
object types counts, and a published $V$ may stand for a $Z$, a $jj$ pair or an $\ell\ell$ pair ---
so the uncovered set is a lower bound on the gap. Two entries are covered only by an $8\TeV$
search and are marked; at $K=2$ nothing is uncovered at all, which is a statement about this
five-object alphabet and not about two-body space, as Table~\ref{tab:twobody} shows.
